title: WPSS/2547/2017 of Rajendra Singh Bisht Vs District And Sessions Judge, Almora

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No.2547 of 2017
Rajendra Singh Bisht Ö.ÖÖ Petitioner
versus
District & Sessions Judge, Almora ÖÖÖ. Respondent
Mr. Arun Pratap Shah, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. Rakesh Thapliyal, Advocate for the respondent.
U. C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
 By means of present writ petition, the petitioner
seeks following reliefs:-
 (i) To issue the writ of certiorari or any other writ, order
or direction for quashing the impugned order dated
07.6.2017 contained in annexure no.1 to the writ
petition.
 (ii) To issue writ of mandamus to respondent to permit
petitioner to sit in the examination for Group ëCí
post.
2. It is a case, in which, learned District Judge,
Almora, relying upon the report of a committee constituted
by him for the purpose of promotion of Group-D employees
to Group-C cadre, dismissed the candidature of the
petitioner on the ground that he is overage. The
committee, it appears, relied upon the Uttrakhand Sub-ordinate Civil Courts Ministerial Establishment Rules,
2007, which is meant for direct recruitment and in which
the age limit is between 21-35 years. Rule 7 of the
aforesaid Rules provides that a candidate for recruitment
to a post in the ministerial establishment must have
attained the age of 21 years and must not have attained
the age of more than 35 on the 1st day of January of the
calendar year in which the vacancies for direct recruitment
are advertised.

-2-
3. Petitioner, admittedly, never applied for direct
recruitment. He is an aspirant for promotion from Group-D to Group-C cadre.
4. Counter affidavit filed by the respondent brings
down curtain on the whole controversy. In para 10 of the
counter affidavit, filed by the respondent, the following has
been mentioned:-
ëÖÖÖÖÖ.that thereafter, vide order dated 27.7.2017, the
District Judge, Almora, suo moto referred the matter to the
committee once again on two issues, namely, on the upper
age limit of Group-D employees to be considered for promotion
to the Group-C employees and pattern of examination.
Committee was directed to submit the report within a week
time. Thereafter, the committee, in its detailed report dated
02.8.2017, informed that in the Rules of 2013, there is no age
limit for Group-D employees to be considered for the
promotion of Group-C employees. In the elaborate report, both
the issues were dealt with by the committee and the report
was submitted to the District Judge, Almora.í
(Emphasis supplied)
5. In para 11 of the counter affidavit it has been
mentioned that the District Judge, Almora, vide order
dated 29.8.2017, directed that the promotion process shall
remain in abeyance till further orders.
6. Thus, it is held that there is no age limit for
Group-D employees to be considered for promotion to
Group-C cadre.
7. Writ petition is allowed. Respondent is directed
to consider the candidature of the petitioner, ignoring the
fact that the upper age limit for consideration of Group-D
employees for promotion to Group-C post is 35 years.

-3-
8. Whole promotional exercise be completed within
a period of twelve weeks from today.
9. Let a copy of this order be sent to District
Judge, Almora, for compliance.
 (U. C. Dhyani, J.)
 23.11.2017
A.kaur
